jury.page.title: Member jury
jury.page.intro: Each month a small panel of members, drawn at random, reviews a sample of closed moderation cases and says whether the decisions fit the rules the co-op voted for. The jury is advisory: it never changes a decision.
jury.disabled.title: The jury is not on
jury.disabled.description: The co-op has not turned the member jury on. Members can propose it as an ordinary decision.
jury.disabled.stillIn: The jury is off, but you are still in its draw. Turn this off to leave it now.
jury.optin.title: Serve on the jury
jury.optin.label: Put me in the monthly draw
jury.optin.on: You are in the draw for the next panel.
jury.optin.off: You are not in the draw.
jury.optin.done: You are in the draw for the next panel
jury.optout.done: You are out of the draw from the next panel
jury.explainer.title: What jurors do
jury.explainer.cases: If you are drawn, you review up to 20 closed cases from the last 30 days over 14 days: the rule that was applied, what was decided, and the evidence the case kept.
jury.explainer.blur: Images are blurred until you choose to reveal each one. Some may be upsetting. The most harmful kinds of case are never shown to jurors.
jury.explainer.names: People appear under a pseudonym that changes every panel. You never see who made a report.
jury.explainer.votes: You agree, disagree or say you are unsure, and pick a reason from a list. There is no free text, and a vote cannot be changed.
jury.explainer.results: Results are published per rule only when at least 10 votes stand behind a figure. A case most jurors disagree with goes back to staff for a second look.
jury.explainer.optout: You can leave the draw at any time with the switch above. Leaving takes effect from the next panel.
jury.ineligible.title: You cannot serve on the jury
jury.ineligible.staff: Platform staff never sit on the jury.
jury.ineligible.notMember: Only active members of the co-op can serve. Join from the membership page.
jury.ineligible.other: Only adult members in good standing can serve.
